Expectation1: Assemble and construct wooden frameworks, furniture, or cabinetry
Situation1: The carpenter is building custom cabinetry and needs to collaborate with other construction professionals to complete the project on time
Expectation2: Support individuals or groups in accessing essential services and resources
Situation2: They encounter a situation where someone urgently needs housing, medical help, or protection and must be connected to services quickly.
Story: I was in the middle of fitting the last panel into a set of custom cabinets, sawdust clinging to my arms, when my phone buzzed. The contractor was already on edge, reminding me that the plumber and electrician were waiting for my part to be done so they could finish their work. The deadline was tight, and any delay would throw the whole project off schedule. As I measured the next piece, another message came through—this time from the shelter coordinator. A family I’d been advocating for had just lost their temporary housing, and the mother was sick. They needed immediate help, someone to connect them to emergency services and a safe place to stay tonight. My mind raced. The crew expected me to stay and finish the cabinetry, to keep the project moving. But the family needed me, too, and I was the only one who knew their story and could speak for them. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in, my hands trembling as I tried to decide which call to answer first.
